header: Continuous sensors or fortnightly hand sampling?
lead: Marnau does both, and is regularly asked why it does not simply pick one. The honest answer is that each method fails in a way the other does not.

points.title: A sensor never misses a night, a storm or a bank holiday.
Fifteen-minute values make short events visible that a fortnightly round cannot see at all.
Once a mast is standing, a year of readings costs almost nothing to collect.
A probe drifts quietly, and a drifting probe produces a plausible series that is simply wrong.
Only four properties can be measured this way; everything biological still needs a bottle.
A hand sample is checked against a laboratory standard on the same day it is taken.
Twelve rounds a year cost more in staff time than the whole sensor network costs to run.
The rounds happen in daylight and in decent weather, which is not when a river is at its most interesting.
